newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bond market seen outperforming Italian Btp.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bond market seen outperforming Italian Btp.

text.p: Bonos are set to outperform their Italian counterparts in the short-term despite a weaker dollar putting a toll on all European peripheral bond markets, analysts said on Tuesday.

With few domestic factors driving the market, Spanish government bonds are likely to follow German bonds down with an unchanged spread over core issues. But Bonos are likely to lose less than Italian Btps, analysts said.
"In the coming days it is likely we will see a widening in the (10-year) spread between Bonos and Italian bonds," said Robert Huw, strategist at Natwest in London.
The dollar/mark plummeted by a pfenning and German Bunds were dumped after comments by German research institutes earlier on Tuesday suggesting a tightening may be on the cards.
Germany's six leading economic research institutes said that interest rates were at appropriate levels now, but added that they should be raised if M3 money supply remained above the target corridor.
In Spain the peseta weakened sharply against the mark, beaten by the dollar's steep slide, and Bonos dropped.
But the 10-year spread over German bunds rose a little, trading at around 179 basis points in the afternoon from 172 basis points at Monday's close.
Btp have risen during the past week, jumping in the immediate aftermath of a surprise official rate cut by Bank of Italy and reducing their spread over the Spanish market to a low of 42 basis points.

After such a rush it is very likely the market will see a widening of that level, said Luis Martin, chief dealer at Deutsche Bank in Madrid. He forecast the spread will widen to 60-65 basis points from around 53 basis points on Tuesday.

Chart analysts in Madrid said all major bond markets were close to support levels, and this could leave Bonos to drop. "Right now the majority of the European markets are close to main support," said one analyst in Madrid.

At 1445 GMT the long-term future contract on Meff was down 19 basis points to 107.25. Initial support is seen at 106.90, then at 106.67. At the same time, the Italian market was down 29 basis points to 122.90.
The peseta was trading at 84.27/30 versus the mark from 84.20/22 in late trading on Monday.
The Spanish market will focus this week on U.S. data, especially third quarter GDP figures due on Wednesday and October payrolls on Friday, dealers said.
